views.name: customer_monthly_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  MIN(txn_date) AS month_first_date,
  MAX(txn_date) AS month_last_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'credit' OR txn_type = 'deposit' OR txn_type = 'CREDIT' OR txn_type = 'Deposit' OR txn_type = 'Credit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_credits,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'debit' OR txn_type = 'withdrawal' OR txn_type = 'DEBIT' OR txn_type = 'Withdrawal' OR txn_type = 'Debit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_debits,
  SUM(CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('debit','withdrawal') THEN -txn_amount ELSE txn_amount END) AS net_txn_amount,
  COUNT(*) AS txn_count
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregate transactions to customer x calendar month level. For each customer-year-month produce total_credits, total_debits, net_txn_amount (sum of signed amounts), txn_count and earliest/latest txn_date within the month. This includes months where transactions exist; joining with a month calendar will be done later to fill gaps.

views.name: customer_monthly_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  printf('%04d-%02d', year, month) AS year_month,
  month AS month,
  year AS year,
  COALESCE(total_credits, 0) AS deposit_sum,
  COALESCE(total_debits, 0) AS withdrawal_sum,
  COALESCE(net_txn_amount, 0) AS net_balance,
  COALESCE(txn_count, 0) AS txn_count
FROM customer_monthly_agg
WHERE year >= 0
grain: one row per customer_id per calendar month (YYYY-MM)
views.description: Per-customer, per-calendar-month aggregated sums of transaction amounts for each txn_type and the net balance for the month. Useful for month-level customer balance, churn, and activity analyses.

views.name: all_customers_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Canonical list of all distinct customer_id values observed in customer transactions. Use as the customer universe to left-join against month-level metrics so months with no transactions count as zero.

views.name: calendar_2020_months
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  2020 AS year,
  m AS month,
  printf('%04d-%02d', 2020, m) AS year_month,
  date(printf('2020-%02d-01', m)) AS month_start_date
FROM (
  SELECT 1 AS m UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL
  SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL
  SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL
  SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12
) months
views.description: Calendar months for year-level analyses. Provides one row per month in 2020 (YYYY-MM). Useful to cross-join with customers to produce all customer-month combinations.

views.name: customer_transactions_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_key,
  lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
  txn_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal', 'withdraw') THEN -txn_amount
    ELSE NULL
  END AS signed_amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  AND lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit', 'withdrawal', 'withdraw')
grain: one row per original customer_transactions row (customer_id, txn_date, txn_type, txn_amount)

semantic_filters.txn_date_format: ISO YYYY-MM-DD assumed; rows with NULL txn_date excluded

views.description: Canonicalized customer transaction rows with parsed ISO txn_date, month_key (first day of month), and signed amount where deposits are positive and withdrawals are negative. Excludes transactions with other txn_type values.

views.name: customer_monthly_nets
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(ct.month_key,1,7) || '-01' AS month_key,
  SUM(ct.signed_amount) AS monthly_net,
  COUNT(*) AS transaction_count
FROM customer_transactions_normalized ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, substr(ct.month_key,1,7) || '-01'
views.description: Per-customer, per-month aggregated net transaction amounts. Each row is one customer + month (month_key = YYYY-MM-01) with monthly_net = sum(signed_amount) and transaction_count.

views.name: customer_transaction_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to YYYY-MM-DD if possible: try common formats using substrings
  -- formats in schema examples: 2020-01-21, 2020-01-10, 01-01-2017, 2017-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, 2020-07-01 00:00:00
  CASE
    WHEN instr(txn_date, 'T') > 0 THEN substr(txn_date, 1, 10)
    WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date, 5, 1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date, 8, 1) = '-' THEN txn_date
    WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date, 3, 1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date, 6, 1) = '-' THEN
      -- convert DD-MM-YYYY or DD-MM-YY to YYYY-MM-DD when possible
      -- assume format DD-MM-YYYY
      substr(txn_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(txn_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(txn_date, 1, 2)
    WHEN instr(txn_date, ' ') > 0 THEN trim(substr(txn_date, 1, instr(txn_date, ' ') - 1))
    ELSE txn_date
  END AS txn_date,
  -- preserve txn_amount as signed value; txn_type may indicate debit/credit but we keep raw txn_amount
  txn_amount,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
grain: one row per customer transaction (customer_id, txn_date, txn_amount)
views.description: Canonical, cleaned transaction-level records for each customer with txn_date normalized as YYYY-MM-DD and txn_amount preserved as signed value. Exposes key identifiers and raw measure columns used for balances and time-based aggregations.

views.name: customer_monthly_cumulative_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.customer_id,
  substr(t.month_key, 1, 7) AS month_year,
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ctn.signed_amount), 0)
    FROM customer_transactions_normalized AS ctn
    WHERE ctn.customer_id = t.customer_id
      AND substr(ctn.month_key, 1, 7) <= substr(t.month_key, 1, 7)
  ) AS balance_cumulative_end_of_month
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, month_key
  FROM customer_transactions_normalized
) AS t
grain: one row per customer per calendar month (end-of-month cumulative)
views.description: Per customer, per-calendar-month cumulative balance up to and including the last day of that month. Each row represents the cumulative balance for a customer as-of the end of a calendar month (YYYY-MM). Useful for computing opening balances on the first day of the next month.

views.name: monthly_total_positive_balances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.month_year AS month_year,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN c.balance_cumulative_end_of_month < 0 THEN 0
      ELSE c.balance_cumulative_end_of_month
    END
  ) AS total_balance_prev_month
FROM
  customer_monthly_cumulative_balance c
JOIN
  (SELECT DISTINCT month_year FROM customer_monthly_cumulative_balance) m
  ON c.month_year = m.month_year
GROUP BY
  m.month_year
views.description: Aggregate monthly view summing per-customer end-of-previous-month balances with negatives floored to zero. Emits one row per month (month_year) representing the month being evaluated (opening balances on its 1st), and the total across all customers after replacing negative balances with 0. Does not exclude the earliest month — exclusion is a question_op.

views.name: customer_txn_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN abs(txn_amount)
    ELSE -abs(txn_amount)
  END AS txn_amount_signed,
  txn_amount AS txn_amount,
  txn_type AS txn_type,
  date(txn_date) AS calendar_date,
  strftime('%Y-%m', date(txn_date)) AS calendar_month
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Canonicalized customer transactions with typed dates, signed amounts (deposits positive, others negative), and calendar month. Keeps one row per source transaction.

views.name: customer_daily_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(ct.txn_date) AS calendar_date,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS daily_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, date(ct.txn_date)
views.description: Per-customer, per-calendar-day aggregated daily running balance computed by ordering transactions by txn_date and cumulatively summing signed txn amounts for that customer on that day. Produces one row per customer-date with the end-of-day running balance.

views.name: customer_daily_30day_rolling_avg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.calendar_date,
  AVG(d.daily_balance) AS rolling_30d_avg
FROM
  customer_daily_balance d
JOIN (
  -- ensure we only consider windows that have at least 30 days present in the 30-day window
  SELECT
    outer_.customer_id AS customer_id,
    outer_.calendar_date AS calendar_date,
    COUNT(inner_.daily_balance) AS days_present_in_window
  FROM customer_daily_balance outer_
  JOIN customer_daily_balance inner_
    ON inner_.customer_id = outer_.customer_id
   AND DATE(inner_.calendar_date) BETWEEN DATE(outer_.calendar_date, '-29 days') AND DATE(outer_.calendar_date)
  GROUP BY outer_.customer_id, outer_.calendar_date
  HAVING COUNT(inner_.daily_balance) >= 30
) w
  ON d.customer_id = w.customer_id
 AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN DATE(w.calendar_date, '-29 days') AND w.calendar_date
GROUP BY
  d.customer_id,
  w.calendar_date
views.description: Per-customer, per-calendar-day 30-day rolling average of daily_balance (includes current day and prior 29 calendar days). Only emits rows where at least 30 days with daily_balance exist in the window. Negative rolling averages are left as-is in this view (question_ops can threshold to 0).

views.name: customer_transaction_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_amount,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  AND txn_date LIKE '____-__-__'
grain: one row per customer_id x original transaction row

semantic_filters.txn_date_format: txn_date LIKE '____-__-__'  -- keep rows that look like YYYY-MM-DD

views.description: Base cleaned transaction rows for each customer: canonical txn_date (YYYY-MM-DD), txn_amount, and txn_type. Filters out NULL or malformed dates and exposes one row per raw transaction.

views.name: customer_daily_txn_summaries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ctr.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to canonical YYYY-MM-DD if possible; assume txn_date already in YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
  substr(ctr.txn_date,1,10) AS txn_date,
  SUM(ctr.txn_amount) AS day_txn_sum,
  COUNT(*) AS day_txn_count
FROM customer_transaction_rows ctr
GROUP BY ctr.customer_id, substr(ctr.txn_date,1,10)
views.description: For each customer and calendar date, the total transaction amount (sum of txn_amount) and count of transactions. Dates are canonical YYYY-MM-DD. One row per customer_id x txn_date.

views.name: customer_date_ranges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn_date,
  MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn_date
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  AND txn_date LIKE '____-__-__'
GROUP BY customer_id
views.description: Per customer calendar date range: min_txn_date and max_txn_date (inclusive). Useful to generate per-customer calendars for carrying forward balances only for relevant spans.

views.name: shopping_cart_event_with_page
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  ph.product_id,
  ph.page_name,
  e.event_type,
  ei.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy ph
  ON e.page_id = ph.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier ei
  ON e.event_type = ei.event_type
WHERE ph.product_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized shopping cart events joined to page hierarchy and event identifier, excluding events that are not tied to a product. Keeps event ordering and raw fields needed to identify views/adds/purchases and to compute per-visit sequencing.

views.name: shopping_cart_event_semantics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.event_type AS event_type,
  ei.event_name AS event_name,
  CASE
    WHEN ei.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1
    WHEN ei.event_name LIKE '%View%' THEN 1
    WHEN ei.event_name IS NOT NULL AND (e.event_type IS NOT NULL AND e.event_type = 1) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_view,
  CASE
    WHEN ei.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1
    WHEN ei.event_name LIKE '%Add%' OR ei.event_name LIKE '%Cart%' THEN 1
    WHEN e.event_type IS NOT NULL AND e.event_type = 2 THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_add_to_cart,
  CASE
    WHEN ei.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1
    WHEN ei.event_name LIKE '%Purchase%' OR ei.event_name LIKE '%Buy%' OR ei.event_name LIKE '%Checkout%' THEN 1
    WHEN e.event_type IS NOT NULL AND (e.event_type = 3 OR e.event_type = 4) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_purchase
FROM shopping_cart_event_identifier ei
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_events e
  ON ei.event_type = e.event_type
GROUP BY ei.event_type, ei.event_name
views.description: Canonical mapping of raw event_type/event_name codes to semantic event categories (view, add_to_cart, purchase). Exposes boolean flags for each semantic type to simplify aggregations and abandonment logic.

views.name: product_event_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.product_id AS product_id,
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.page_name AS "page_name as product_name",
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.visit_id AS visit_id,
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.event_time AS event_time,
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.sequence_number AS sequence_number,
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.event_type AS event_type,
  shopping_cart_event_with_page.event_name AS event_name
FROM shopping_cart_event_with_page
WHERE shopping_cart_event_with_page.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  AND shopping_cart_event_with_page.product_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Raw event-level cohort for product-linked events (filtered for product_id present and excluding irrelevant page_ids). Keeps visit-product-event ordering to support downstream aggregations: counts of views/adds/purchases and detection of add-without-later-purchase per visit-product.

views.name: interest_monthly_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  interest_id,
  month_year,
  _month,
  _year,
  composition,
  index_value,
  (composition / index_value) AS composition_over_index
FROM interest_metrics
WHERE index_value IS NOT NULL AND index_value != 0
views.description: Canonical monthly interest-level metrics with cleaned month/year identifiers and numeric measures. One row per interest_id per month.

views.name: interest_id_to_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  im.interest_id AS interest_id,
  COALESCE(i.interest_name, CAST(im.interest_id AS TEXT)) AS interest_name
FROM interest_metrics im
LEFT JOIN interest_map i
  ON CAST(im.interest_id AS INTEGER) = i.id
GROUP BY im.interest_id, i.interest_name
views.description: Mapping of interest_id to human-readable interest_name (falls back to id as text if no mapping). Exposes canonical name for downstream reporting.

views.name: monthly_top_interest_candidates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  imm.month_year AS month_year,
  imm.interest_id AS interest_id,
  imm.composition_over_index AS composition_over_index,
  MAX(imm.composition_over_index) OVER (PARTITION BY imm.month_year) AS monthly_max_composition_over_index,
  CASE WHEN imm.composition_over_index = MAX(imm.composition_over_index) OVER (PARTITION BY imm.month_year) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_monthly_top
FROM interest_monthly_metrics imm

semantic_filters.month_year: NULL (no hard-coded month filter here; filter applied in question_ops)

views.description: For each month, compute the per-interest composition_over_index and the per-month maximum composition_over_index. One row per interest_id per month plus an indicator of whether it equals the monthly max.

views.name: interest_metrics_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(interest_id AS INTEGER) AS interest_id,
  NULL AS interest_name_candidate,
  month_year AS month_year,
  printf('%02d-%04d', CAST(_month AS INTEGER), CAST(_year AS INTEGER)) AS month_year_mm_yyyy,
  composition AS composition,
  index_value AS index_value,
  ranking AS ranking,
  percentile_ranking AS percentile_ranking
FROM interest_metrics
WHERE composition IS NOT NULL
grain: interest_metrics.interest_id -- one row per original metric record
views.description: Normalized / cleaned interest_metrics rows: canonical month-year string, numeric interest_id where possible, and non-null composition and index_value. Keeps one row per original interest_metrics record.

views.name: interest_map_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  interest_name,
  interest_summary,
  created_at,
  last_modified
FROM interest_map
grain: interest_map.id -- one row per interest category
views.description: Core interest categories from interest_map with stable id and canonical name. Exposes id and interest_name for joins and display.

views.name: interest_max_composition_per_interest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(imc.interest_id, NULL) AS interest_id_numeric,
  imc.interest_name_candidate AS interest_name,
  imc.composition AS max_composition,
  imc.month_year_mm_yyyy AS month_year_mm_yyyy_at_max
FROM interest_metrics_clean imc
JOIN (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(interest_id, NULL) AS interest_id_inner,
    COALESCE(interest_name_candidate, interest_id) AS interest_identity,
    MAX(composition) AS max_comp
  FROM interest_metrics_clean
  WHERE composition IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY interest_identity
) m
  ON COALESCE(imc.interest_id, NULL) = m.interest_id_inner
  AND imc.composition = m.max_comp
WHERE imc.composition IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per interest_id_numeric + month_year_mm_yyyy_at_max (ties preserved)
interest_id_numeric or fallback to interest_name for identification
views.description: For each interest (as identified by numeric id when available, otherwise by name candidate), compute the maximum composition across months and capture the month_year(s) when that maximum occurred. Keeps measures raw and keeps ties as multiple rows so final ranking can decide tie behavior.

views.name: bitcoin_transactions_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  txn_id,
  member_id,
  ticker,
  txn_date AS txn_date_raw,
  -- normalize common date formats to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible
  -- try formats: DD-MM-YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, MM-DD-YYYY
  (CASE
     WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' THEN
       -- assume DD-MM-YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD
       substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
     WHEN instr(txn_date, '/') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '/' THEN
       -- assume DD/MM/YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD
       substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
     WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-' THEN
       -- assume already YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-M-D variants; take first 10 chars
       substr(txn_date,1,10)
     ELSE
       NULL
   END) AS txn_date_iso,
  -- extract calendar year from normalized ISO date
  (CASE
     WHEN
       (CASE
         WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' THEN
           substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
         WHEN instr(txn_date, '/') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '/' THEN
           substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
         WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-' THEN
           substr(txn_date,1,10)
         ELSE
           NULL
        END) IS NOT NULL
     THEN CAST(substr(
       (CASE
         WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' THEN
           substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
         WHEN instr(txn_date, '/') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '/' THEN
           substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
         WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-' THEN
           substr(txn_date,1,10)
         ELSE
           NULL
        END),1,4) AS INTEGER)
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS calendar_year,
  txn_type,
  quantity,
  txn_time
FROM bitcoin_transactions
WHERE
  -- intrinsic filters: require parsed ISO date, quantity, and txn_type present
  txn_type IS NOT NULL
  AND quantity IS NOT NULL
  AND
  (CASE
     WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' THEN
       substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
     WHEN instr(txn_date, '/') > 0 AND length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '/' THEN
       substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
     WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-' THEN
       substr(txn_date,1,10)
     ELSE
       NULL
   END) IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonicalized bitcoin transactions filtered to valid BUY/SELL rows with a parsed calendar year and normalized date format so they can be joined to bitcoin_prices; keeps raw quantity and txn_type and member id for joins to members.

views.name: bitcoin_prices_by_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date AS market_date_raw,
  -- Normalize market_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD when possible. Many market_date values are DD-MM-YYYY per schema examples.
  CASE
    WHEN length(trim(market_date)) = 10 AND substr(market_date,3,1) = '-' AND substr(market_date,6,1) = '-' THEN
      -- assume DD-MM-YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD
      substr(market_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(market_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(market_date,1,2)
    WHEN length(trim(market_date)) = 10 AND substr(market_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(market_date,8,1) = '-' THEN
      -- assume YYYY-MM-DD already
      market_date
    ELSE
      NULL
  END AS market_date_iso,
  CAST(price AS REAL) AS price
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE price IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    (length(trim(market_date)) = 10 AND substr(market_date,3,1) = '-' AND substr(market_date,6,1) = '-')
    OR (length(trim(market_date)) = 10 AND substr(market_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(market_date,8,1) = '-')
  )
grain: ticker, market_date_iso -- one row per ticker per market date
views.description: Normalized bitcoin price table with a canonical date field (ISO or YYYY) and numeric price for joining to transactions by ticker+date. Keeps original market_date and price.

views.name: member_region
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  member_id,
  region
FROM bitcoin_members
WHERE member_id IS NOT NULL
  AND region IS NOT NULL
views.description: Lookup of bitcoin member id to member region. Exposes member id and the region name for joins and grouping. Excludes members with NULL member_id or NULL region to simplify downstream joins.

views.name: bitcoin_volume_numeric
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date,
  -- try to parse market_date into ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) if it's in DD-MM-YYYY; otherwise pass through NULL for unknown formats
  (CASE
     WHEN instr(market_date, '-') = 3 THEN
       -- format like DD-MM-YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD
       substr(market_date, 7, 4) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(market_date, 4, 2) AS INTEGER)) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(market_date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER))
     ELSE
       NULL
   END) AS market_date_iso,
  volume,
  -- normalized numeric volume: handle '-', trailing K/k or M/m, plain numbers with optional commas
  (CASE
     WHEN trim(volume) = '-' OR volume IS NULL OR trim(volume) = '' THEN 0.0
     ELSE
       -- remove commas and percent signs and whitespace
       (CASE
         WHEN lower(trim(volume)) LIKE '%m' THEN
           -- remove trailing M and any non-numeric chars, convert to number * 1,000,000
           CAST(replace(replace(replace(trim(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume))-1)), ',', ''), ' ', ''), 'K', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
         WHEN lower(trim(volume)) LIKE '%k' THEN
           CAST(replace(replace(replace(trim(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume))-1)), ',', ''), ' ', ''), 'M', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
         ELSE
           -- try plain numeric after removing commas; if not numeric, yield 0.0
           (CASE
              WHEN replace(trim(volume), ',', '') GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN CAST(replace(trim(volume), ',', '') AS REAL)
              ELSE 0.0
            END)
       END)
   END) AS volume_numeric,
  -- flag rows where volume is '-' or null or empty -> true (1), otherwise false (0)
  (CASE WHEN trim(volume) = '-' OR volume IS NULL OR trim(volume) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS volume_is_zero
FROM bitcoin_prices
grain: market_date -- one row per ticker per market_date (original string)
views.description: Converts bitcoin_prices.volume text into a numeric volume value (raw units) and a flag for zero/unknown. Handles '-', trailing K/k or M/m multipliers, and plain numeric values. Exposes volume_numeric for each ticker+date for reuse.

views.name: ticker_prior_nonzero_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.ticker AS ticker,
  v.market_date AS market_date,
  v.market_date_iso AS market_date_iso,
  v.volume_numeric AS volume_numeric,
  (
    SELECT bp.market_date_iso
    FROM bitcoin_volume_numeric bp
    WHERE bp.ticker = v.ticker
      AND bp.market_date < v.market_date
      AND bp.volume_numeric IS NOT NULL
      AND bp.volume_numeric != 0
    ORDER BY bp.market_date DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS prior_market_date_iso,
  (
    SELECT bp.volume_numeric
    FROM bitcoin_volume_numeric bp
    WHERE bp.ticker = v.ticker
      AND bp.market_date < v.market_date
      AND bp.volume_numeric IS NOT NULL
      AND bp.volume_numeric != 0
    ORDER BY bp.market_date DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS prior_volume_numeric
FROM bitcoin_volume_numeric v
grain: market_date -- one row per ticker per market_date with prior non-zero volume if exists
views.description: For each ticker and market_date provides the most recent prior market_date (strictly earlier) with a non-zero converted volume and its volume_numeric. Useful for computing percent change relative to last available non-zero volume.

views.name: veg_loss_items
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  item_code,
  item_name,
  "loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate_pct
FROM veg_loss_rate_df
WHERE "loss_rate_%" IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical row-level view of vegetable wholesale items with numeric loss rate. Exposes item identifier, item name and a cleaned numeric loss_rate_pct suitable for aggregation. Filters out rows where loss rate is NULL.

views.name: veg_loss_rate_aggregates_per_itemset
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(item_code) AS total_items,
  AVG(loss_rate_pct) AS avg_loss_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(item_code) <= 1 THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- sample standard deviation: sqrt( SUM((x - mean)^2) / (n-1) )
      SQRT( (SUM(loss_rate_pct * loss_rate_pct) - (SUM(loss_rate_pct) * SUM(loss_rate_pct)) / COUNT(item_code)) / (COUNT(item_code) - 1) )
  END AS stddev_loss_rate
FROM
  veg_loss_items
grain: single row per aggregation (whole table or filtered subset when WHERE applied externally)
views.description: Pre-aggregated loss-rate summary measures over a provided item set (no WHERE baked in). Computes count, average loss rate, and sample standard deviation of loss_rate_pct. Intended as reusable aggregation for summaries and comparisons.

views.name: veg_loss_items_with_deviation_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.item_code AS item_code,
  v.item_name AS item_name,
  v.loss_rate_pct AS loss_rate_pct,
  agg.avg_loss_rate AS avg_loss_rate,
  agg.stddev_loss_rate AS stddev_loss_rate,
  CASE WHEN v.loss_rate_pct < agg.avg_loss_rate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_below_mean,
  CASE WHEN v.loss_rate_pct > agg.avg_loss_rate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_above_mean,
  CASE WHEN ABS(v.loss_rate_pct - agg.avg_loss_rate) <= COALESCE(agg.stddev_loss_rate, 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_within_one_stddev
FROM veg_loss_items v
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT
    AVG(loss_rate_pct) AS avg_loss_rate,
    -- SQLite uses a user-defined stddev; approximate with population stddev via sqrt(avg(x^2)-avg(x)^2)
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(loss_rate_pct) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE sqrt( (AVG(loss_rate_pct * loss_rate_pct)) - (AVG(loss_rate_pct) * AVG(loss_rate_pct)) )
    END AS stddev_loss_rate
  FROM veg_loss_items
  WHERE loss_rate_pct IS NOT NULL
) agg
WHERE v.loss_rate_pct IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per item_code with analytic measures and boolean flags
views.description: Item-level view that annotates each item with the overall mean and stddev (from table) and flags indicating relation to mean and one-standard-deviation band. Mean/stddev are computed over the full table unless a WHERE is applied externally before this view is materialized.

views.name: veg_transactions_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(veg_txn_df."index", NULL) AS txn_id,
  veg_txn_df.txn_date AS txn_date,
  veg_txn_df.txn_time AS txn_time,
  veg_txn_df.item_code AS item_code,
  veg_txn_df."qty_sold(kg)" AS qty_sold_kg,
  veg_txn_df."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS unit_selling_px_rmb_per_kg,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', substr(veg_txn_df.txn_date,1,10)) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year
FROM veg_txn_df
WHERE veg_txn_df."qty_sold(kg)" IS NOT NULL
  AND veg_txn_df."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', substr(veg_txn_df.txn_date,1,10)) AS INTEGER) IN (2020,2021,2022,2023)
grain: one row per veg_txn_df transaction record

semantic_filters.exclude_nulls: qty_sold_kg IS NOT NULL AND unit_selling_px_rmb_per_kg IS NOT NULL

views.description: Cleaned and normalized vegetable transactions with parsed calendar year and non-null price/quantity. Keeps one row per transaction event exposing item, datetime, quantity and selling unit price plus derived calendar_year.

views.name: veg_wholesale_yearly
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  item_code,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
  AVG("whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS avg_whsle_px,
  MAX("whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS max_whsle_px,
  MIN("whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS min_whsle_px,
  SUM("whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS sum_whsle_px,
  COUNT("whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS count_whsle_records
FROM veg_whsle_df
WHERE "whsle_px_rmb-kg" IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS INTEGER) IN (2020,2021,2022,2023)
GROUP BY item_code, CAST(strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Wholesale price records normalized with parsed calendar_year and aggregated per item_code x calendar_year. Exposes per-item-year average, min, max, sum and count of wholesale price records. Excludes NULL wholesale prices and restricts to target years.

views.name: veg_item_category_loss
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  vc.item_code AS item_code,
  vc.category_name AS category_name,
  COALESCE(vl."loss_rate_%", 0.0) AS loss_rate_pct
FROM veg_cat vc
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT item_code, category_name
  FROM veg_cat
  WHERE category_name IS NOT NULL
) vc_nonnull ON vc.item_code = vc_nonnull.item_code
LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df vl
  ON vc.item_code = vl.item_code
WHERE vc.category_name IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per item_code (only items that have a category_name)
views.description: Denormalized mapping of veg item -> category and loss rate with loss_rate defaulted to 0 when missing. Exposes item_code, category_name and loss_rate_pct for use in aggregation and monetary loss calculations.

views.name: weekly_sales_canonical_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date_raw,
  -- Try ISO YYYY-MM-DD (assume already valid), else try DD/MM/YYYY or DD/MM/YY
  (CASE
    WHEN instr(week_date, '-') = 5 AND length(week_date) >= 10 AND substr(week_date,5,1) = '-' THEN week_date
    WHEN instr(week_date, '/') > 0 AND length(week_date) = 10 THEN
      -- DD/MM/YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD
      substr(week_date,7,4) || '-' || printf('%02d', cast(substr(week_date,4,2) AS INTEGER)) || '-' || printf('%02d', cast(substr(week_date,1,2) AS INTEGER))
    WHEN instr(week_date, '/') > 0 AND length(week_date) = 8 THEN
      -- DD/MM/YY -> assume 20YY for years 00-69 => 2000-2069, 70-99 => 1970-1999 (common two-digit rule)
      (CASE
        WHEN cast(substr(week_date,7,2) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 0 AND 69 THEN '20' || substr(week_date,7,2)
        ELSE '19' || substr(week_date,7,2)
      END) || '-' || printf('%02d', cast(substr(week_date,4,2) AS INTEGER)) || '-' || printf('%02d', cast(substr(week_date,1,2) AS INTEGER))
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS week_date_iso,
  -- derive calendar_year from parsed ISO when available
  (CASE
    WHEN
      (instr(week_date, '-') = 5 AND length(week_date) >= 10 AND substr(week_date,5,1) = '-')
      THEN cast(substr(week_date,1,4) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN instr(week_date, '/') > 0 AND length(week_date) = 10 THEN cast(substr(week_date,7,4) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN instr(week_date, '/') > 0 AND length(week_date) = 8 THEN
      (CASE
        WHEN cast(substr(week_date,7,2) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 0 AND 69 THEN cast('20' || substr(week_date,7,2) AS INTEGER)
        ELSE cast('19' || substr(week_date,7,2) AS INTEGER)
      END)
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS calendar_year,
  region,
  platform,
  segment,
  customer_type,
  transactions,
  sales
FROM weekly_sales
WHERE
  -- keep only rows where we could parse into one of the supported formats
  (
    (instr(week_date, '-') = 5 AND length(week_date) >= 10 AND substr(week_date,5,1) = '-')
    OR (instr(week_date, '/') > 0 AND (length(week_date) = 10 OR length(week_date) = 8))
  )
grain: one row per original weekly_sales row
views.description: Normalize and canonicalize weekly_sales.week_date into ISO YYYY-MM-DD dates where possible, expose original fields and numeric sales/transactions. Keeps rows that can be parsed into a date in common formats (ISO YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YY or DD/MM/YYYY).

views.name: weekly_sales_by_day_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  wsc.week_date_iso AS week_date_iso,
  wsc.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  wsc.region AS region,
  wsc.platform AS platform,
  wsc.segment AS segment,
  wsc.customer_type AS customer_type,
  wsc.transactions AS transactions,
  wsc.sales AS sales
FROM weekly_sales_canonical_dates wsc
WHERE wsc.week_date_iso IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per weekly_sales record (with canonical date)
views.description: Row-level cohort view that exposes weekly_sales rows with parsed ISO date and common dimensions so callers can filter by arbitrary date ranges (inclusive) and aggregate sales/transactions. Does not aggregate; kept at original row granularity.

views.name: calendar_period_boundaries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  y.year AS year,
  date(y.june15, '-28 days') AS pre_period_start_date,
  date(y.june15) AS pre_period_end_date,
  date(y.june16) AS post_period_start_date,
  date(y.june16, '+27 days') AS post_period_end_date
FROM (
  SELECT
    cast(years.year AS INTEGER) AS year,
    printf('%04d-06-15', cast(years.year AS INTEGER)) AS june15,
    printf('%04d-06-16', cast(years.year AS INTEGER)) AS june16
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT cast(substr(txn_date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM customer_transactions
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', week_date) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM weekly_sales
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', start_date) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM shopping_cart_users
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', market_date) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM bitcoin_prices
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', month_year) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM interest_metrics
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT cast(substr(start_date,1,4) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM shopping_cart_campaign_identifier
  ) AS years
) AS y
views.description: Generate canonical pre/post 28-day period boundary dates around June 15 for a given calendar year. Exposes start and end ISO dates for pre-period (28 days ending on June 15) and post-period (28 days starting June 16). Useful for joining with date-normalized sales rows.

views.name: cleaned_weekly_sales_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cleaned_weekly_sales.week_date AS week_date,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.week_date_formatted AS week_date_formatted,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.week_number AS week_number,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.month_number AS month_number,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.region AS region,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.platform AS platform,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.segment AS segment,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.age_band AS age_band,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.demographic AS demographic,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.customer_type AS customer_type,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.transactions AS transactions,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.sales AS sales,
  cleaned_weekly_sales.avg_transaction AS avg_transaction
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
WHERE cleaned_weekly_sales.sales IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per cleaned_weekly_sales.week_date + original dimensional combination
views.description: Canonicalized weekly sales rows with ISO week_date, calendar year/week/month fields and cleaned numeric sales/transactions; one row per original cleaned_weekly_sales record. Keeps the key dimensions commonly used for segmentation (region, platform, segment, age_band, demographic, customer_type) and the canonical week_date for time-window membership.

views.name: weekly_sales_by_dimension_period
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  'region' AS dimension_name,
  region AS dimension_value,
  week_date AS week_start_date,
  SUM(sales) AS sales_weekly
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY week_date, region

UNION ALL

SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  'platform' AS dimension_name,
  platform AS dimension_value,
  week_date AS week_start_date,
  SUM(sales) AS sales_weekly
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY week_date, platform

UNION ALL

SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  'age_band' AS dimension_name,
  age_band AS dimension_value,
  week_date AS week_start_date,
  SUM(sales) AS sales_weekly
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY week_date, age_band

UNION ALL

SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  'demographic' AS dimension_name,
  demographic AS dimension_value,
  week_date AS week_start_date,
  SUM(sales) AS sales_weekly
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY week_date, demographic

UNION ALL

SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  'customer_type' AS dimension_name,
  customer_type AS dimension_value,
  week_date AS week_start_date,
  SUM(sales) AS sales_weekly
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY week_date, customer_type
views.description: Aggregates total sales per dimension value per ISO week_date. This view produces weekly sales series per attribute value and is intended to be used to sum sales across arbitrary date ranges (pre/post windows). It exposes dimension_name and dimension_value so the same view can be used for region, platform, age_band, demographic, or customer_type aggregations.

views.name: dimension_period_compare_aggregate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  wsd.dimension_name,
  wsd.dimension_value,
  SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.pre_period_start_date AND cpb.pre_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) AS pre_period_sales,
  SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.post_period_start_date AND cpb.post_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) AS post_period_sales,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.pre_period_start_date AND cpb.pre_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.post_period_start_date AND cpb.post_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) AS REAL)
          - CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.pre_period_start_date AND cpb.pre_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) AS REAL)
         )
         / CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.pre_period_start_date AND cpb.pre_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) AS REAL) * 100
  END AS pct_change
FROM weekly_sales_by_dimension_period wsd
CROSS JOIN calendar_period_boundaries cpb
GROUP BY
  wsd.dimension_name,
  wsd.dimension_value
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN wsd.week_date BETWEEN cpb.pre_period_start_date AND cpb.pre_period_end_date THEN wsd.sales_weekly END) IS NOT NULL
views.description: For a chosen reference date and period lengths, computes aggregated pre_period_sales and post_period_sales for each (dimension_name, dimension_value). Excludes dimension values with pre_period_sales = 0 to avoid division by zero. Also computes the pct_change per dimension value = (post - pre)/pre * 100. This is a parameterizable view: date boundaries and period lengths should be applied in question_ops when used.
